title: Evidence Chain Format
description: Canonical format for evidence chain entries. Every entry links to its predecessor via hash. Chains are append-only, verifiable, and stored in PGlite as the authoritative store.

chain_id.description: Unique identifier for this evidence chain

hash.description: SHA-256 hash of this entry's content

predecessor_hash.description: SHA-256 hash of the previous entry. Null for the chain genesis entry.

signature.description: Ed25519 signature over (entry_id + timestamp + hash + predecessor_hash + entry_type)

signer.description: Identity of the signer (principal or service identity)

metadata.description: Free-form metadata specific to the entry type

integrity_proof.description: Proof that the chain has not been tampered with

chain_hash.description: Merkle root of all entry hashes

invariants: Append-only: no entry may be removed or modified after appending. Any removal or modification breaks the hash chain.
Chaining: every entry except the genesis entry must reference the hash of its immediate predecessor.
Verifiability: any party with the public key of the signer can verify each entry's signature.
Durability: evidence chains are stored in PGlite (RecoveryReceiptTable, WorkAttemptTable, DeadLetterTable) as the authoritative store.
Replay: the entire evidence chain for a work item can be reconstructed from PGlite rows alone — no external state needed.
